By the summer of 1942, Nazi Germany and its allies controlled almost every inch of continental Europe.

On this map only five countries stayed neutral, and Britain sits alone in dark blue off the coast.

Europe at the Axis high-water mark — a thread 🧵🗺️

1/ The black core is the German Reich itself. By 1942 that already absorbed Austria, the Czech lands, western Poland, Luxembourg, Alsace-Lorraine and part of Slovenia — annexed outright rather than merely occupied.

2/ Dark grey is occupation: Norway, Denmark, the Netherlands, Belgium, northern France, Greece, Serbia and the vast conquered belt of the western USSR. Each had its own regime — some military, some civilian, all extractive.

3/ Mid-grey marks allies, co-belligerents and puppet states: Italy, Hungary, Romania, Bulgaria, Slovakia, Croatia and Finland. Romania and Hungary both sent armies east against the USSR while quietly competing for Transylvania behind Germany's back.

4/ Finland is the odd one out. It fought the Soviets alongside Germany from 1941 but kept its parliament, its elections and its own war aims. Finns called it the Continuation War — a separate conflict that happened to share an enemy.

5/ Neutral green: Sweden, Switzerland, Spain, Portugal and Turkey. Neutrality was rarely pure. Sweden sold Germany iron ore, Swiss banks and rail tunnels stayed open, and Franco sent Spanish volunteers to the Eastern Front.

6/ Vichy France holds the palest shade — "nominally unoccupied." That ended in November 1942: within days of the Allied landings in North Africa, German troops moved into the southern zone. The map was obsolete almost as soon as it peaked.

7/ Three years after this snapshot, the black core was rubble and the Soviet red on the right-hand edge had reached Berlin.
